question.:question/problem:
Consider the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}5 & -1 & -7 \\ 4 & 7 & -3 \\ 8 & 6 & 8\end{bmatrix}.
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{3}:=-2{R}_{3}$ on $A?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The operation ${R}_{3}:=-2{R}_{3}$ means that we need to multiply the third row of the matrix by $-2.$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}5 & -1 & -7 \\ 4 & 7 & -3 \\ 8 & 6 & 8\end{bmatrix}\quad {R}_{3}:=-2{R}_{3} \\ & \sim \begin{bmatrix}5 & -1 & -7 \\ 4 & 7 & -3 \\ -2\cdot (8) & -2\cdot (6) & -2\cdot (8)\end{bmatrix} \\ & \sim \begin{bmatrix}5 & -1 & -7 \\ 4 & 7 & -3 \\ -16 & -12 & -16\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}-6 & 9 & 0 \\ 4 & 9 & 2 \\ 0 & -9 & 3\end{bmatrix}\quad {R}_{3}:=2{R}_{3} \\ & \sim \begin{bmatrix}-6 & 9 & 0 \\ 4 & 9 & 2 \\ 2\cdot (0) & 2\cdot (-9) & 2\cdot (3)\end{bmatrix} \\ & \sim \begin{bmatrix}-6 & 9 & 0 \\ 4 & 9 & 2 \\ 0 & -18 & 6\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}6 & 6 & 0 \\ -2 & -9 & 1 \\ -6 & 2 & 7\end{bmatrix}.
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{1}:=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1}$ on $A?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The operation ${R}_{1}:=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1}$ means that we need to multiply the first row of the matrix by $-\frac{1}{3}.$

Multiplying the first row by $-\frac{1}{3}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}6 & 6 & 0 \\ -2 & -9 & 1 \\ -6 & 2 & 7\end{bmatrix}\quad {R}_{1}:=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\ & \sim \begin{bmatrix}-\frac{1}{3}\cdot (6) & -\frac{1}{3}\cdot (6) & -\frac{1}{3}\cdot (0) \\ -2 & -9 & 1 \\ -6 & 2 & 7\end{bmatrix} \\ & \sim \begin{bmatrix}-2 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & -9 & 1 \\ -6 & 2 & 7\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$
